messages.content: 尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。

function.name: find_movie_showing
function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find two movie theaters near San Diego that have showtimes at 5pm for Tenet and 7:30pm for No Time To Die. We need to use the function find_movie_showing. The function signature expects location: string, movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], time: string[]. So we need to call the function twice? Actually we need to find two theaters. The function can return multiple theaters? It returns any. We can call it with location "San Diego, CA", movie "Tenet", time ["17:00"] to get theaters showing Tenet at 5pm. Then call again with movie "No Time To Die", time ["19:30"]. But the user wants two theaters that provide both showtimes? Or two separate theaters each with one of those showtimes? The phrasing: "尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。" Means "Find two movie theaters near San Diego that offer a 5pm showing of Tenet and a 7:30pm showing of No Time To Die." Could be interpreted as find two theaters that each have both showtimes. But maybe they want two theaters: one for Tenet at 5pm, another for No Time To Die at 7:30pm. The phrase "兩家電影院" means two theaters. "提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次" could mean each theater provides those showtimes. But ambiguous.

We can interpret as find two theaters that each have both showtimes. That would be more useful. So we need to call function twice? Actually we can call function once with movie array? The function signature: movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[]; time: string[]. So we can pass movie array ["Tenet", "No Time To Die"], time array ["17:00", "19:30"]. That might return theaters that have both showtimes. Let's do that. We'll call find_movie_showing with location "San Diego, CA", movie ["Tenet", "No Time To Die"], time ["17:00", "19:30"].
